evidence: Confirmed, narrowed to the unresolved decision rule rather than an absence of any safeguard. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:18 adopts retirement on live pane/tab/workspace closure and explicitly leaves cascading closure and external cleanup unspecified. DESIGN-NOTES.md:147 expressly leaves last-pane/containing-tab behavior and reliable closure-versus-unavailable-observation distinction open; :157 proposes that an incomplete snapshot cannot prove deliberate closure and that graph-issued closures need correlation, but this is labeled an unapproved consequence, not a complete rule. Full-text search of all four artifacts for close/closure, retire/archive, cascade, unavailable/missing/snapshot, ambiguity, and recovery found directional safeguards at DESIGN-NOTES.md:125,157,166,197-198 and HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:33,92-94, yet no adopted evidence threshold or descendant-scope mapping. The missing contract is material to the stated requirement that ordinary manual Herdr changes feed graph state while preserving correct organizational identity (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:33,54,94,139). A last-pane observation or transiently incomplete workspace view could otherwise be interpreted at the wrong scope; this is a prospective design risk, not a claim of actual data loss or a demand for perfect observation. The accepted best-effort allowance for missed actions (DESIGN-NOTES.md:180) does not settle classification of an observed ambiguous action.
